articles.title: SPEC Acid Carbon Mesh
articles.summary: Tight gloss cells over matte under-weave; acid-tinted carbon mesh with crisp micro contrast. Disappears into a plain base finish with a slightly textile sheen; no acid colour appears, since a spec only changes shine.
articles.what: Acid-tinted mesh/carbon contrast with tight gloss cells and matte under-weave. Up close: Ultra-fine diagonal crosshatch, thin lines crossing at right angles a few pixels apart, like a screen mesh or woven fabric seen under raking light. Faint on satin, visible as a shimmering lattice in the metallic highlight and as dark cross-hatch in the shadow floor. From a distance: Disappears into a plain base finish with a slightly textile sheen; no acid colour appears, since a spec only changes shine. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Source Pattern Plates (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Source Pattern Plates", or search for "SPEC Acid Carbon Mesh".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof: broad flats show the shimmer
Metallic bases where the mesh is visible
No effect on legibility; numbers read as normal.
Hardly visible, a faint woven fuzz in the highlight
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic.
pitfalls: Not acid or green paint: no tint, the name's acid is not a colour in a spec
Not big carbon twill: weave is much finer, a mesh crosshatch
Avoid: subtle at distance, acid tint may clash with warm liveries.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
